transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-29 14:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Claire Huang (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Nadia Patel (CSM) — Priya Nair (Trenchline Head of Platform), Ethan Cole (NetOps), Lucia Park (SRE), TomÃ¡s Rivera (Security)

Summary:
Quick midweek sync to review the last 48h of telemetry after the egress shaping changes, discuss the kernel/quant upgrade timing, and confirm the next canary cutover window. Focus was on routing anomalies (two small spikes), fallback behavior and proving KMS handshake in the private pilot.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Claire: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we have like 47 minutes on the invite so we'll try to keep this tight. quick roll call?
[00:12] Priya: priya here, lucia, ethan and tomas are with me. thanks for squeezing us in.
[00:18] Claire: awesome, claire from redwood, marcus my se, nadia is on for ops and support. quick agenda: telemetry readout, egress shaping effects, kernel/quant upgrade plan, kms handshake, then next steps.
[00:35] Marcus: i'll start with the telemetry — we pulled 48 hours post-shaping. overall token cost dropped ~6% on average, batching improved median token throughput. there were two small tail spikes around 03:20 and 08:10 UTC that correlate with a large request fanout from your agent cluster.
[01:02] Ethan: yeah that was a scheduled downstream retrain job that fans out a lot of small requests — we thought it was isolated but looks like it rippled. did you see any circuit breaker trips?
[01:12] Marcus: we observed one CB trip at 03:22, it auto-failed over to the hosted fallback for about 42 seconds. logs show KV cache miss rate went up which increased per-token cost briefly.
[01:28] Lucia: that matches our local traces, we saw a small increase in tail latency p99s at the same time. not huge, but visible.
[01:35] Claire: good to know — did fallback behave as expected? any authentication or KMS errors during that time?
[01:43] Marcus: no auth errors. the fallback used the hosted model endpoint; because you have prefix caching enabled the responses were slightly higher cost but correct. no KMS handshake happened since the hosted fallback uses Redwood-managed keys.
[01:59] TomÃ¡s: that's the thing we wanted to avoid long-term — we need assurances fallback doesn't leak any sensitive metadata and that audit logs show the failover. do you provide end-to-end audit traces?
[02:14] Nadia: yes, we have audit logs for each request including routing decision and fallback reason. we'll share a sample trace after this call.
[02:25] Priya: perfect. another thing — the egress shaping seemed to reduce tail but increased jitter for the small requests. can you explain that tradeoff?
[02:36] Marcus: it's expected — shaping batches micro-requests to squeeze GPU utilization; that reduces average cost but for super small requests the queuing adds jitter. we can tune the micro-batching threshold to prioritize latency for those, i.e. lower batch window but accept higher cost.
[02:53] Ethan: can we have a per-route config? some routes are user-facing and need low tail latency, others are internal async jobs.
[03:02] Claire: yes, per-route policies are available — you can pin a low-latency SL to those routes and leave others on cost-optimized batching. we'll send a suggestion for the policy mapping after we see your route list.
[03:16] Lucia: noted. about the kernel/quant upgrade you proposed last week — what's the compatibility matrix again? we run an nvlink-enabled onprem cluster with A100s and some older T4 nodes for preproc.
[03:31] Marcus: the new quant path supports A100 and A10x, and has a graceful fallback for older cards using the previous kernels. on mixed clusters we recommend pinning A100-heavy model shards to avoid cross-architecture penalties. we should validate on your hybrid testbed.
[03:48] TomÃ¡s: is there any chance the new kernels will change inference outputs, or is it strictly performance?
[03:55] Marcus: in most cases it's performance/bit-width changes for quantization; outputs are equivalent within expected float quant noise. we'll include a small eval suite to check for regression on your prompts.
[04:10] Priya: ok — when can you run that eval?
[04:13] Marcus: we can schedule the regression run during the burn test (planned 1000 concurrent tokens). claire will coordinate the window.
[04:21] Claire: speaking of the burn test, we propose a 3h window 2026-07-02 02:00-05:00 UTC — is that acceptable?
[04:30] Ethan: yes that's doable, but we'll need the exact IPs and a pre-provisioned VPC peer to be in place.
[04:37] Claire: noted, action for ethan to provision.
[04:40] [05:00] Marcus: jumping back to the routing spikes — i looked at the path selection logs, and the spike was caused by a combination of an unexpected request fanout and our sticky routing timeouts not clearing. small TTL on the route cache plus a transient DNS blip sent some traffic to a less optimal region.
[05:17] Lucia: we had a DNS CNAME update during that window; didn't think it would affect connections but apparently it did. can sticky TTLs be adjusted?
[05:25] Marcus: yes, we can increase route sticky TTL for your tenant to 30s or even 60s to avoid re-routing churn during known dns changes. downside is slower adaptation to genuine topology changes.
[05:41] Priya: sounds fine for now. also want to confirm telemetry retention window — we need 90 days for audit.
[05:48] Nadia: audit retention add-on is available; we can enable 90-day retention for your pilot account with export hooks to your S3.
[05:58] TomÃ¡s: about KMS — we tested a handshake with your dev env before and got an intermittent error: "invalid key handle". did you look into that?
[06:08] Marcus: yes, that was due to a mismatch in key aliases between your HSM and the Redwood test key mapping. we'll need the alias mapping and your KMS provider endpoint. TomÃ¡s, can you share that?
[06:18] TomÃ¡s: i'll paste it to the shared doc after this call.
[06:22] Claire: reminder — for private deployments we support customer-managed keys via our KMS proxy; in some setups there's a short TTL for key leases which can produce transient errors under heavy parallelism. we can bump the lease if needed.
[06:36] Ethan: good to know. latency regressions: we saw p95 move from 120ms to 165ms during the spike, p99 to 1.2s. is that within expected behavior?
[06:47] Marcus: p99 being 1.2s is above our target; that's why we want to run the burn test and the kernel eval. after egress shaping tuning and increasing sticky TTLs we predicted p99 below 900ms.
[06:59] Lucia: what about cache priming? you mentioned prefix/KV caching earlier — can we pre-warm some keys for the retrain job?
[07:08] Marcus: yes, we can seed the KV with the top-500 prefixes you expect; that should cut misses and reduce early spike cost. we'll accept a list of prefixes from you.
[07:18] Priya: we'll assemble that and upload.
[07:21] [08:00] Claire: switching to security concerns — audit logs, encryption, and consent. TomÃ¡s are you ok with the audit sample nadia will send?
[08:10] TomÃ¡s: yes, send it. we need to validate fields: request id, routing decision, key alias, fallback reason, timestamp. also need to ensure no PII is logged.
[08:22] Nadia: we'll strip PII and provide request id mapping.
[08:26] TomÃ¡s: perfect. also need to run a small key rotation test. can that be done during the same window?
[08:34] Marcus: rotations are safe but they add another variable to the burn test; recommend doing rotation afterwards in a controlled test.
[08:43] Priya: agreed, let's keep burn window focused.
[08:46] [09:00] Claire: ok timeline recap — burn test 2026-07-02 02:00-05:00 UTC; Marcus runs kernel/regression and uploads evals; ethan provisions VPC peer and shares IPs; claire sends security pack and price. anything else?
[09:18] Priya: one ask — can we have a small SLA table for the pilot only? e.g., latency SLOs and what counts as failover.
[09:25] Claire: yes we can produce a pilot SLA doc, non-contractual but actionable. will include SLOs, escalation, rollback triggers.
[09:34] Lucia: we also need a clear rollback playbook if the kernel upgrade causes correctness regressions.
[09:40] Marcus: we have a rollback channel; we'll keep model version pinning for a quick flip. rollback is just a routing switch and re-deploy to previous kernel path.
[09:52] Ethan: do you support canary by user percentage or only by route?
[09:57] Marcus: both. you can do a percentage split by route or pin by tenant id. for your test we'll do a 5% ring first.
[10:06] [10:30] Priya: about cost — the observed 6% reduction is nice, but micro-requests still cost more. can you show a break-down by route and token-length?
[10:39] Marcus: yes, we'll produce a CSV with per-route cost, median token length and hit rates.
[10:44] Claire: and we can overlay it with the per-route policy recs.
[10:49] TomÃ¡s: competitor question — we were evaluating Hyperserve's model - are there feature gaps we should be aware of?
[10:58] Claire: hyperserve focuses on simple endpoints but lacks per-tenant sticky routing and integrated KV prefix caching tuned for LLM prefix patterns. XenonRuntime provides something similar but without the audit+kms proxy stack. we'll write a short comparison note.
[11:16] Lucia: thanks. small nit — how do you handle connection resets mid-kv-stream? we had a test where the streaming pipe closed and the client retried, ending up with duplicates.
[11:29] Marcus: we provide idempotency tokens and idempotent chunk markers for streaming; you can enable dedup on your client side. we'll share the guidance doc.
[11:38] [12:00] Priya: ok can we talk about the canary cutoff? if we see a p99 > 1s at 5% ring, do we abort automatically?
[12:09] Marcus: we can set automatic abort thresholds — yes, if p99 exceeds configured threshold for X minutes we auto-rollback. we'll propose thresholds in the pilot SLA doc.
[12:20] Ethan: what about alerts — will we get an immediate page for CB trips or fallback events?
[12:25] Nadia: we'll configure pagerduty hooks and a slack channel for routing events.
[12:31] Lucia: good. we also want a short runbook for oncall — who to call at redwood for urgent kernel rollbacks?
[12:38] Claire: i'll include primary and secondary SE contacts in the runbook.
[12:42] [13:00] Marcus: quick technical note — the KV cache TTL defaults might cause thrash under high churn; we recommend an adaptive TTL setting which we can enable for your tenant. it will lengthen TTL during stable periods and shorten during high fanout bursts.
[13:14] Priya: that sounds useful. enable it for the burn test?
[13:18] Marcus: yes we can.
[13:20] [14:00] TomÃ¡s: any outstanding legal/procurement blockers? we have procurement loops but pilot is under existing eval terms.
[14:27] Claire: no new legal required for the pilot; if you convert to dedicated we'll need an amended contract.
[14:34] Priya: ok good.
[14:36] [15:00] Claire: let's capture the decisions: 1) increase route sticky TTL to 30s for tenant 7092 during the burn test. 2) enable adaptive KV TTL. 3) run quant/kernel regression during burn. 4) pilot SLA doc and audit sample to be shared.
[15:53] Ethan: confirmed.
[15:55] Marcus: i'll run the regression and upload by 2026-07-01.
[16:00] [16:30] Priya: last question — can you simulate our agent fanout pattern or do we need to run it from our side?
[16:40] Marcus: we can simulate if you provide an approximated request distribution. for fidelity we'll want you to run the canonical fanout from within your network; that helps exercise your egress path.
[16:53] Lucia: we'll run it from our side during the burn.
[16:58] Claire: perfect. anything else?
[17:02] TomÃ¡s: one more thing — we want a short post-burn report with three sections: performance, correctness, and security. can you commit to that?
[17:11] Claire: yes, we'll produce a post-burn report within 48h of the test.
[17:16] Priya: great. thanks everyone.
[17:19] Claire: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and action items.
[17:24] Meeting ends.
